```{r message = F}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
set.seed(1)
```

# Problem 1 

## Write a function to assess birthday overlap in a room of `n` people. 

```{r}
source("source/birthday_overlap.R")
```

## Run the function 10,000 times for group sizes of 2 - 50 people. 

```{r}
birthday_results_df = 
  expand_grid(
    number_of_people = 2:50, 
    iter = 1:10000 
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    repeated = map_lgl(number_of_people, birthday_overlap)
  )
```

## Plot showing the probability of birthday overlap as a function of group size 

```{r}
birthday_results_df |> 
  group_by(number_of_people) |> 
  summarize(prob_of_repeat = mean(repeated)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = number_of_people, y = prob_of_repeat)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line()  +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of Shared Birthdays in Different Group Sizes", 
    x = "Number of People", 
    y = "Probability of Shared Birthday") +
  theme_minimal()
```

In a room of 23 people, there is a ~50% chance that two people will share a birthday. This probability increases steadily as the number of people in the room increases. 

# Problem 2

## Make a dataframe with all file names

```{r}
participants_df = 
  tibble(
    file_name = list.files(path = "data", full.names = TRUE)
    ) 
```

## Iterate over file names and read in data for each participant 

```{r}
data_import = function(file) {
  
  data_df = 
    read_csv(file = file) |> 
    janitor::clean_names() |> 
    pivot_longer(
      week_1:week_8,
      names_to = "week", 
      values_to = "data"
      ) |> 
    mutate(
      week = str_replace(week, "week_", ""), 
      week = as.numeric(week))
  
  return(data_df)
  }
```

```{r message = F}
participants_df =
  participants_df |> 
  mutate(
    data = map(file_name, data_import)) |> 
  unnest() 
```

## Tidy the result 

```{r}
participants_df =
  participants_df |> 
   mutate(
     file_name = str_replace(file_name, ".csv", ""), 
     file_name = str_replace(file_name, "data/", ""), 
     subject_id = file_name
   ) |> 
  separate(file_name, into = c("arm", "id"), sep = "_")
```

## Make a spaghetti plot showing observations of each subject over time

```{r}
participants_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = data, group = subject_id, color = arm)) +
  geom_line()
```

The observations of participants in the experimental arm of the study have higher data points than the control arm. Additionally, there seems to be a slight increasing trend in the experimental group over the 8 weeks of observation. 

# Problem 3 

## Exploring power using a function 

```{r}
t_test_power = function(n = 30, mu = 0, sigma = 5) {
  
  x = rnorm(n = n, mean = mu, sd = sigma)
  
  t.test(x, mu = 0) |> 
    broom::tidy() |> 
    select(estimate, p.value)
  
}
```

## Generate 5000 datasets 

```{r}
t_test_results_df =  
  expand_grid(
    mu = 0,
    iter = 1:5000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    results = map(mu, \(m) t_test_power(n = 30, mu = m, sigma = 5))
  ) |> 
  unnest(results)
```

## Repeating when mu = 1:6 

```{r}
t_test_results_df =  
  expand_grid(
    mu = 1:6,
    iter = 1:5000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    results = map(mu, \(m) t_test_power(n = 30, mu = m, sigma = 5))
  ) |> 
  unnest(results)
```
